Communicare - Housing Invasion by Gangs

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
The Cops stood by and watched as a group of gangster invade a social housing project owned and managed by Communicare in Brooklyn . Security guards were attacked with bottles, bins were burnt, doors to tenants’ apartments were broken and cars were damaged by the crowd who were intent to violently occupy the vacant units. Members of the crowd threatened some tenants and said they would return to burn down the units and set tenants alight. SAPS stood by and watched all this unfold and refused to take any action despite pleas from tenants and Communicare. In one incident SAPS instructed a security guard to allow the illegal occupiers to move into the vacant units. Then two weeks later they tried at another housing unit Drommedaris but this time the security guards were able to defend the property and the Brooklyn police eventually arrived two hours later but not before staff had petrol bombs throw at them

Summary:
Communicare has experienced attempts to illegally occupy the units at Goedehoep Rental Complex in Brooklyn since 2 March. At the time the illegal occupations were reported to Maitland Police by they refused to take any action to protect property and legal tenants. SAPS failure resulted in escalating violence and 24 apartments in the complex being occupied by the trespassers. Several violent scuffles broke out between a group of about 40 people led by 2 tenants from another of Communicare’s properties

They have now hijacked the building have now drilled holes through the walls of legal residents to gain access to their electricity and have dug up the mains to get to the water. The legal tenants are mostly old people and single mothers. They are also being intimidated to leave. Communicare tried to improve their security guards at the complex this Saturday but police again interfered and they had to retreat. A petrol bomb was thrown at the security guards yesterday.[this was captured on video}

The SAPS have said Communicare must oppose the occupation by applying under Prevention of Illegal Eviction and Unlawful Occupation of Land Act 19 of 1998 (PIE). However the people who were trespassing are not tenants or occupants being removed, they were storming the properties in the presence of SAPS and terrorising the tenants. The Communicare security guards attempted to prevent the trespassers from resorting to violence to enter the property however SAPS refused to intervene. Now they hoping to get a court order to eject them with an exploitation order, if that fails then evicting them could take years. The law does not stand on the side of property owners, once somebody has gained access to the property its virtually impossible to get them out.


Further information:
The City of Cape Town is doing nothing to assist, mayor Dan Plato has simply said the law must change but this has nothing to do with eviction of people who can’t pay rent, it’s is straight criminal behaviour. The gangs at the gate are getting the new tenants to pay them R900 a unit. One of the theories is that the gangs are not getting sufficient protection money from businesses so are resorting to capturing residential properties

We have footage of the incident and voice notes from terrified residents and people are willing to be interviewed if we hide their identity.



Extra Budget Items:
We will need security for the crew - gangs are operating the complex. The Communicare security consultant will watch our backs but we may need additional security which we will have to pay for

Script:


Script: There is a growing trend across Cape Town of people illegally occupying properties counting on Covid disaster regulations to protect them from eviction. Once they’re in they hope the lengthy court action using the Prevention of Illegal eviction Act- PIE will protect them
Link It’s a property owners worst nightmare. People storm the gate and forcibly gain entry access, once they are in it can take months or even years to get them out
Script: This complex was stormed by women and children, using gangsters to beat back the security and gain access to 24 unoccupied apartments, in a complex run by Communicare, a not for profit organization in Cape Town. Communicare’s social rental units provide subsidised rentals for low- income families and pensioners. CEO Anthea Houston explains their relationship to government housing
Anthea “ Anyone involved with housing delivery has to work with government because there's a lot of permissions that one needs to deliver housing. So we do work with government, but we're not part of government, we're not a government agency
Script: In early March people broke into one of the vacant apartments at Goedehoop in the middle of the night assisted by residents who live in the building. Over the next few days 18 more units were occupied. Mohamed Samsodien the Communicare facilities manager reported the trespassing to the local police station.

Samsodien: we went to SAPS and we opened tried to open the case out of which it wasn’t of any help. We then headed out to Cape Town to get the attention of the cluster commanded in Cape Town , but nothing actually expired from that

Script: Then on the night of the 12th March all hell broke loose. The illegal occupants started arriving in taxi loads led by residents from another complex. Burning bins outside the gates they tried to force security to let them bring in their furniture. Adiel November is in charge of security at Goedehoop, says it was many hours before the police arrived
Adiel: these people forced their way through the gates they beat up security guards. and they forced their way and they forced the furniture into the unit. In the presence of SAPS while SAPS was doing totally, totally nothing. I was literally in tears asking them, please help. I'm giving you authority. Come inside, this is crime up in front of you? Why can't we help us? Why can't you act against these people? And I was totally ignored.

Script: Goedhoop has many elderly residents, and they were terrified

V: It's terrible and you didn't know what to do, huh?
Mac: What are the people doing? what was happening
V: They were using whatever they could to break the gates down, the one flat and windows was smashed in,
Mac: what the security doing at this point in time, where were they?
V: Security couldn't do anything,

Script: When we asked the police for an interview they replied - the allegations levelled at SAPS are not only without basis, but also unfair. The matter you are referring to is being dealt with in ongoing meetings with the stakeholders

Script: A few days after that violent night Communicare tried to evict the illegal occupiers with the help of the Red ants but were attacked. This time the police arrived in 20 minutes

Samsodien SAPs actually informed us to leave the complex and to leave these people,. And then also when we tried to negotiate with these people on getting access, again,. Saps they didn't step up as we expected them to.

Script: The South African Police says “interventions are conducted within the framework of the law and we are not in the position to evict illegal occupiers of buildings. This is the responsibility of the court.“

Anthea: The law is very clear on it. It's not fuzzy. It's there's no covid regulations stopping anyone from removing tresspasses caught in the act of trespassing. It was very clear on that evening that it was not a place of residence for the people who were storming in there. And so we do feel that the police failed us and they failed the tenants who live there lawfully

Script: The police failed to respond to our further requests for an interview

Adiel: Now, these guys had gangsters protecting the gates. So they were offered you you help we give half the complexes. So it's all organised syndicate operating there
ANTHEA The people who illegally occupied have declined to sit down with us at any point. And they they are not leaseholders they don't pay us rent. We've heard rumors that they were paying some folks rent. We don't know who those people are. And we also don't know on what basis they're collecting money from from people who live in those apartments now. 09:40:33:18 it's really about sort of establishing a syndicate or an operation in which poor people and the need for housing can be extorted.

Link So for the past 3 weeks this gate has been operated by the illegal occupiers and communicare who are the rightful owners have been prevented from even coming in
Samsodien “ I cannot send in any of the maintenance teams contractors, service providers, anybody out to this complex . The current residents also are living in fear at the moment. 12:33:17:22 people are drilling through the walls to connect up their power and water from the units into these illegal occupied units.

“I am not safe”

Script: Voice notes like this haunt the staff who feel completely helpless

“I have just been beaten up by 6 women they say they going to throw petrol bombs, I cant to live here anymore

E: All the time there is alcohol, shouting, screaming, partying. You don't feel like you should be walking around

Mac: Do do we know where they come from? I mean seem to be driving quite fancy cars from what you've experienced,

E: very fancy cars. so I'm not sure where they have cars. They're trying to get free housing and coming in and trying to take over a complex like that

Script: Then two weeks later at Drommedaris, another Communicare complex- the next occupation was planned. Ntombuzuko Kraai and a group of women, who was also active in the Goedehoop invasion, held a protest at Drommedaris. They were objecting to the new security company which Communicare had hired who were better defended against these attacks.

Veronica: that night was we felt like hostages, The security guards were standing outside the gate. Um, they were loud music like in a club or something. People chantering And then I think around 8:00 oclock, it started to become very worse People started walking around the building

“Windows broken”

Script: While the protest was happening at the front gate, unoccupied units were broken into

V2 “People are breaking inside the building. And it was so scary

Script: This time the Milnerton police backed up Communicare security and the occupation failed. Mahommed inspected the damage with the help of the police

Samsodien “ And as I was about to leave the complex, they actually assaulted me. “

Script: It was Communicare security who pulled the women off Mohammed. He now needs an operation to remove bone fragments from his shoulder

Samsodein: At first they hijacked the unit and they put these poorer people in these unit, and most of the time it's women, children,..., and they get told how to perform or how to react should we come out to remove them? And that's by undressing themselves and screaming, abuse or things to that, and then head off to the police station and open cases against us.

Mac: so of using this gender based violence., as a tactic to do this.

Samsodien “There we go

Link So we had arranged an interview with the Drommedaris Pilot Project beneficiaries and this was to hear their side of the story
Script “But enroute we discovered this whatsapp using our interview to organised a protest. We asked Ntombuzuko Kraai to withdraw it, initially she agreed but then sent this voice message
Voice note
Script: Albert Fritz is the MEC of Community safety in the Western Province, his department doesn't have operational powers, but has a parliamentary oversight role
Fritz: So we've also asked that the police ombudsman investigate the matter more fully as a neutral independent 09:46:20:05 - that culture of not wanting to pay, that culture of getting everything for free that we must resolve and that bridge where housing entities want to survive, but it also reasonable rents.

Script: Almost a month after the invasion Communicare applied for an urgent spoliation order which argues that the occupiers are trespasses and were never legal residents, circumventing the Prevention of Illegal Eviction Act-PIE. Attorney Marlon Shevelew explains the predicament Communicare find themselves in

Marlon if you're faced with a situation where people moving in unlawfully, you want to approach this court as a matter of great urgency because delaying it means you invariably will find yourself before a court in terms of PIE application, which brings in a whole range of section twenty six of the Constitution, right to housing and all the factors that actual unlawful occupiers are allowed to bring in to seek the protection of our courts

Script: Court proceedings were delayed by 3 weeks to allow the occupiers time to prepare legal argument. The judge did however order the security access to be returned to Communicare, with the assistance of the police. Xolani Newu who spoke for the Goedehoop occupiers in court agreed to an interview but then never showed up, referring us to these women, who were evasive

Mac 4.42 T why would Communicare want to remove people and go to court, if they are there legally

Fatima “ I don't care who is being removed. Do it the proper way…...I don't ask for papers from anyone. Unless you want someone out go to the court, obtain an eviction order and you can have that person thrown out

Script: Currently 45 units of Communicare’s social housing have been illegally occupied, and evictions can take years. The damage to the buildings is already over R250 000 to say nothing of the millions spent on increased security, at all the complexes
